nodes.title: FET Phase
nodes.description: Further Education and Training Phase (Grades 10-12)

nodes.title: Life Sciences
nodes.description: Life Sciences — Grade 11 — CAPS Curriculum

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: SBA: Practical task and test. Weeks 1–11.

nodes.title: Biodiversity and Classification of Micro-organisms
nodes.description: Basic structure, characteristics and roles of viruses, bacteria, protista and fungi; symbiotic relationships; disease management; immunity and drugs.

nodes.title: Viruses — structure and characteristics
nodes.description: Basic structure and characteristics of viruses; non-cellular nature; lytic and lysogenic cycles (overview).

nodes.title: Bacteria — structure and characteristics
nodes.description: Basic structure and characteristics of bacteria; prokaryotic cell; symbiotic relationships including nitrogen-fixing bacteria and E. coli.

nodes.title: Protista — structure and characteristics
nodes.description: Basic structure and characteristics of protista; eukaryotic; roles in environment.

nodes.title: Fungi — structure and characteristics
nodes.description: Basic structure and characteristics of fungi; saprophytic nutrition; roles in environment.

nodes.title: Roles of micro-organisms in the environment
nodes.description: Decomposition, nitrogen fixation, food chains; positive and negative roles of micro-organisms in ecosystems.

nodes.title: Symbiotic relationships
nodes.description: Symbiotic relationships involving micro-organisms: nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume root nodules; E. coli in the human gut.

nodes.title: Effect and management of disease
nodes.description: Effect and management of one disease caused by each group: viral, bacterial, protistan, and fungal diseases. Prevention and control strategies.

nodes.title: Immunity, drugs, antibiotics and vaccinations
nodes.description: Concept of immunity; how antibiotics and vaccines work; antibiotic resistance; role of drugs in disease management.

nodes.title: Micro-organisms in medicine and traditional technology
nodes.description: Beneficial uses of micro-organisms: production of antibiotics, vaccines, fermented foods, traditional medicines and biotechnology applications.

nodes.title: Biodiversity of Plants
nodes.description: Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms; vascular tissue, seeds/spores, fruit; asexual and sexual reproduction; flowers; pollination adaptations.

nodes.title: Bryophytes
nodes.description: Characteristics of bryophytes: no vascular tissue, no true leaves or roots, reproduce by spores, high water dependence. Examples: mosses and liverworts.

nodes.title: Pteridophytes
nodes.description: Characteristics of pteridophytes: vascular tissue present, true leaves and roots, reproduce by spores, still water dependent for fertilisation. Examples: ferns.

nodes.title: Gymnosperms
nodes.description: Characteristics of gymnosperms: vascular tissue, true leaves and roots, naked seeds (no fruit), reduced water dependence. Examples: conifers, cycads.

nodes.title: Angiosperms
nodes.description: Characteristics of angiosperms: vascular tissue, true leaves and roots, seeds enclosed in fruit, least water dependent. Monocots vs dicots.

nodes.title: Decreasing water dependence across plant groups
nodes.description: Evolutionary trend from bryophytes to angiosperms: progressive reduction in dependence on water for reproduction and survival; adaptations to terrestrial life.

nodes.title: Asexual and sexual reproduction in plants
nodes.description: Asexual reproduction methods (vegetative propagation, runners, tubers, bulbs, cuttings). Sexual reproduction involving alternation of generations (overview); gametophyte and sporophyte generations.

nodes.title: Flowers as reproductive structures
nodes.description: Structure and function of flower parts: sepals, petals, stamens (anther, filament), carpel (stigma, style, ovary, ovule). Role in sexual reproduction.

nodes.title: Pollination adaptations
nodes.description: Adaptations for wind, insect and bird pollination with South African examples. Structural features of flowers that attract specific pollinators.

nodes.title: Biodiversity of Animals
nodes.description: Concept of phylum; six phyla: Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata; key features; role of invertebrates in agriculture and ecosystems.

nodes.title: Concept of phylum and key classification features
nodes.description: Definition of phylum; key features used to classify animals: body symmetry, tissue layers, gut openings, coelom, blood systems.

nodes.title: Phylum Porifera
nodes.description: Key features of sponges: no true tissues, asymmetry, filter feeders, water canal system. Examples and ecological roles.

nodes.title: Phylum Cnidaria
nodes.description: Key features of cnidarians: radial symmetry, two tissue layers, one gut opening, cnidocytes. Examples: jellyfish, sea anemones, coral.

nodes.title: Phylum Platyhelminthes
nodes.description: Key features of flatworms: bilateral symmetry, three tissue layers, acoelomate, one gut opening. Examples: tapeworms, flukes. Disease significance.

nodes.title: Phylum Annelida
nodes.description: Key features of segmented worms: bilateral symmetry, three tissue layers, coelom, two gut openings, closed blood system. Examples: earthworms, leeches. Role in soil aeration.

nodes.title: Phylum Arthropoda
nodes.description: Key features of arthropods: exoskeleton, jointed appendages, segmented body, open blood system. Classes: Insecta, Arachnida, Crustacea, Myriapoda. Agricultural and ecosystem roles.

nodes.title: Phylum Chordata
nodes.description: Key features of chordates: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail. Overview of vertebrate classes: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals.

nodes.title: Role of invertebrates in agriculture and ecosystems
nodes.description: Beneficial roles: pollination, decomposition, soil aeration, food chains. Harmful roles: crop pests, disease vectors. Pest management strategies.

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: SBA: Assignment and June examination. Weeks 1–11.

nodes.title: Photosynthesis
nodes.description: Process of photosynthesis in words and symbols; raw materials, energy trapping, food formation, oxygen release; light and dark phases; factors affecting rate; ATP as energy carrier.

nodes.title: Overview of photosynthesis
nodes.description: Overall process of photosynthesis expressed in words and chemical symbols: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy → C6H12O6 + 6O2. Raw materials: carbon dioxide, water, light. Products: glucose and oxygen.

nodes.title: Light phase and dark phase (overview)
nodes.description: Light phase: light absorbed by chlorophyll, water photolysis, ATP and NADPH production, oxygen released. Dark phase (Calvin cycle): CO2 fixed, glucose synthesised using ATP and NADPH. Mention only — no biochemical detail required.

nodes.title: ATP as an energy carrier
nodes.description: Role of ATP as the universal energy currency in cells; synthesis during light phase; release of energy during hydrolysis to ADP + Pi.

nodes.title: Importance of photosynthesis
nodes.description: Foundation of most food chains; oxygen production; carbon dioxide removal; basis of fossil fuels; importance to life on Earth.

nodes.title: Factors affecting rate of photosynthesis
nodes.description: Effects of light intensity, CO2 concentration, and temperature on the rate of photosynthesis. Limiting factors concept. Interpretation of graphs.

nodes.title: Greenhouse systems and controlled environments
nodes.description: Use of greenhouse technology to optimise photosynthesis: manipulation of light, CO2, temperature and humidity for increased food production.

nodes.title: Cellular Respiration
nodes.description: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration; glycolysis, Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation (overview); lactic acid fermentation; industrial applications; comparison of aerobic and anaerobic.

nodes.title: Aerobic respiration — overview
nodes.description: Overall equation for aerobic respiration: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy (ATP). Occurs in mitochondria. Releases maximum ATP.

nodes.title: Glycolysis
nodes.description: Glycolysis: glucose split into two pyruvate molecules in the cytoplasm; net gain of 2 ATP; no biochemical detail required.

nodes.title: Krebs cycle
nodes.description: Krebs cycle: pyruvate converted to acetyl-CoA; entry into the citric acid cycle in the mitochondrial matrix; CO2 released; ATP and electron carriers produced. No biochemical detail required.

nodes.title: Oxidative phosphorylation
nodes.description: Oxidative phosphorylation: electron transport chain on inner mitochondrial membrane; large ATP yield; oxygen as final electron acceptor; water produced. No biochemical detail required.

nodes.title: Anaerobic respiration — lactic acid fermentation
nodes.description: Anaerobic respiration in animals and some bacteria: pyruvate converted to lactic acid; small ATP yield; oxygen debt; muscle fatigue. Industrial uses: yoghurt production.

nodes.title: Anaerobic respiration — alcoholic fermentation and industrial use
nodes.description: Alcoholic fermentation in yeast: pyruvate → ethanol + CO2; industrial applications in bread-making, brewing and biofuel production.

nodes.title: Comparison of aerobic and anaerobic respiration
nodes.description: Comparison: location, oxygen requirement, ATP yield, end products, efficiency. Tabular comparison of aerobic vs anaerobic respiration.

nodes.title: Animal Nutrition
nodes.description: Dentition; human alimentary canal; ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion; chemical digestion enzymes; hepatic portal system; homeostatic control of blood sugar.

nodes.title: Dentition
nodes.description: Types of teeth and dental formulae in herbivores, carnivores and omnivores. Relationship between tooth structure and diet. Comparison of dentition.

nodes.title: Structure of the human alimentary canal
nodes.description: Organs of the alimentary canal: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum), large intestine, rectum, anus. Associated glands: salivary, liver, pancreas.

nodes.title: Ingestion and mechanical digestion
nodes.description: Ingestion: taking food into the mouth. Mechanical digestion: chewing, churning in stomach, peristalsis; increases surface area for enzymatic digestion.

nodes.title: Chemical digestion — enzymes
nodes.description: Chemical digestion by enzymes: carbohydrases (amylase, maltase), proteases (pepsin, trypsin), lipases. Sites of action, substrates and products. Role of bile in emulsification.

nodes.title: Absorption — structure of villi
nodes.description: Absorption in the small intestine; structure and function of villi and microvilli; surface area adaptations; absorption of glucose, amino acids into blood; fatty acids and glycerol into lacteals.

nodes.title: Assimilation and egestion
nodes.description: Assimilation: use of absorbed nutrients by body cells for energy, growth and repair. Egestion: removal of undigested material as faeces via the rectum and anus.

nodes.title: Hepatic portal system
nodes.description: Hepatic portal vein carries absorbed nutrients from small intestine to the liver. Liver functions: regulation of blood glucose, deamination, detoxification, bile production, storage of glycogen.

nodes.title: Homeostatic control of blood sugar
nodes.description: Role of insulin and glucagon in regulating blood glucose levels; glycogenesis and glycogenolysis; role of the pancreas and liver; diabetes mellitus (Type 1 and Type 2) as a disruption of homeostasis.

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: SBA: Practical task and test. Weeks 1–11.

nodes.title: Gaseous Exchange
nodes.description: Distinction between cellular respiration, breathing and gas exchange; human ventilation system; gaseous exchange in alveoli and tissues; gas transport; homeostatic control of breathing.

nodes.title: Distinguishing cellular respiration, breathing and gas exchange
nodes.description: Cellular respiration: chemical process releasing energy from glucose. Breathing (ventilation): mechanical movement of air into and out of lungs. Gas exchange: diffusion of O2 and CO2 across respiratory surfaces.

nodes.title: Requirements for efficient gas exchange
nodes.description: Large surface area, thin membrane, moist surface, good blood supply, maintenance of concentration gradient.

nodes.title: Structure of the human ventilation system
nodes.description: Organs: nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli, lungs, diaphragm, intercostal muscles, pleural membranes. Structure and function of each.

nodes.title: Mechanism of ventilation
nodes.description: Inhalation: diaphragm contracts and flattens, external intercostal muscles contract, thoracic volume increases, pressure decreases, air flows in. Exhalation: reverse process.

nodes.title: Gaseous exchange in alveoli and tissues
nodes.description: Diffusion of O2 from alveoli into blood and CO2 from blood into alveoli. Diffusion of O2 from blood into tissues and CO2 from tissues into blood. Concentration gradient maintenance.

nodes.title: Transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide in blood
nodes.description: Oxygen transport: oxyhaemoglobin formation in red blood cells. Carbon dioxide transport: dissolved in plasma, as bicarbonate ions, as carbaminohaemoglobin.

nodes.title: Homeostatic control of breathing rate
nodes.description: Role of medulla oblongata (respiratory centre) in detecting CO2 levels in blood; feedback mechanism adjusting breathing rate; chemoreceptors.

nodes.title: Excretion in Humans
nodes.description: Excretory organs; urinary system; kidney structure and function; nephron processes; homeostatic control via ADH and aldosterone.

nodes.title: Excretory organs and their excretory products
nodes.description: Lungs: CO2 and water vapour. Kidneys: urea, uric acid, salts, water. Liver: bile pigments (bilirubin). Skin: water, salts, urea via sweat. Alimentary canal: bile pigments in faeces.

nodes.title: Structure of the urinary system
nodes.description: Organs: kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra. Gross structure of the kidney: cortex, medulla, pelvis, renal artery, renal vein, ureter.

nodes.title: Structure of the nephron
nodes.description: Parts of the nephron: Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, collecting duct. Associated blood supply.

nodes.title: Ultrafiltration
nodes.description: High pressure filtration in the glomerulus: water, glucose, urea, salts, amino acids forced into Bowman's capsule. Large molecules (proteins, blood cells) remain in blood.

nodes.title: Selective reabsorption
nodes.description: Reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, water and some salts from proximal convoluted tubule and loop of Henle back into blood. Active transport and osmosis mechanisms.

nodes.title: Tubular secretion
nodes.description: Active secretion of additional waste products (H+ ions, some drugs, creatinine) from blood into the tubule filtrate in the distal convoluted tubule.

nodes.title: Homeostatic control — ADH and aldosterone
nodes.description: ADH (antidiuretic hormone): released by hypothalamus/posterior pituitary; increases water reabsorption in collecting duct; regulates blood osmolarity. Aldosterone: released by adrenal cortex; increases Na+ reabsorption; regulates blood volume and pressure.

nodes.title: Population Ecology
nodes.description: Population size factors; growth curves; population interactions; human population growth.

nodes.title: Factors affecting population size
nodes.description: Natality (birth rate), mortality (death rate), immigration, emigration. Carrying capacity of the environment. Biotic and abiotic limiting factors.

nodes.title: Population growth curves
nodes.description: Logistic (S-shaped/sigmoid) growth curve: lag, exponential and plateau phases; effect of carrying capacity. Geometric (J-shaped) growth curve: exponential growth without limiting factors. Interpretation and comparison.

nodes.title: Predation
nodes.description: Predator–prey relationships; cyclical fluctuations in population size; co-evolution of predator and prey adaptations. Examples from South African ecosystems.

nodes.title: Competition
nodes.description: Intraspecific competition (within a species) and interspecific competition (between species) for food, space and mates. Competitive exclusion principle.

nodes.title: Specialisation
nodes.description: Niche specialisation as a mechanism to reduce interspecific competition; resource partitioning; examples of niche differentiation in South African ecosystems.

nodes.title: Parasitism
nodes.description: Parasitism: one organism (parasite) benefits at the expense of the host. Ectoparasites and endoparasites. Examples: ticks, tapeworms. Effect on host population.

nodes.title: Mutualism and commensalism
nodes.description: Mutualism: both species benefit (e.g., oxpecker and rhino, clownfish and anemone). Commensalism: one species benefits, the other is unaffected. South African examples.

nodes.title: Human population growth
nodes.description: Historical and projected human population growth; factors driving growth (medicine, agriculture, sanitation); demographic transition model; impact on resources and environment; sustainability.

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: SBA: End-of-year examination. Weeks 1–10.

nodes.title: Human Impact on the Environment
nodes.description: Atmosphere and climate change; water availability and quality; food security; loss of biodiversity; solid waste disposal.

nodes.title: Atmosphere and climate change
nodes.description: Greenhouse effect: role of CO2, methane and other greenhouse gases; carbon footprint; global warming consequences. Ozone layer depletion: causes (CFCs) and effects (UV radiation increase).

nodes.title: Water availability and quality
nodes.description: Freshwater scarcity; pollution of water sources (industrial, agricultural, domestic); eutrophication; water purification; sustainable water use in South Africa.

nodes.title: Food security
nodes.description: Global and South African food security challenges; causes of food insecurity (population growth, drought, conflict); sustainable agriculture; GMOs; food waste.

nodes.title: Loss of biodiversity — sixth extinction
nodes.description: Current mass extinction event; causes: habitat destruction, invasive species, pollution, overexploitation, climate change. Consequences. Conservation strategies: protected areas, legislation, rehabilitation.

nodes.title: Solid waste disposal
nodes.description: Types of solid waste (domestic, industrial, hazardous); landfill impacts; incineration; recycling and waste reduction (reduce, reuse, recycle); e-waste; sustainable waste management.

nodes.title: Revision and Final Examination
nodes.description: Revision week followed by end-of-year examination. Paper 1 (150 marks): Photosynthesis 32, Animal nutrition 32, Respiration 22, Gaseous exchange 32, Excretion 32. Paper 2 (150 marks): Biodiversity micro-organisms 29, Plants 29, Animals 18, Population ecology 37, Human impact 37.

nodes.title: Revision
nodes.description: Structured revision of all Term 1–4 topics in preparation for the final examination.

nodes.title: Paper 1 — Life Processes
nodes.description: End-of-year Paper 1 (150 marks): Photosynthesis (32), Animal nutrition (32), Cellular respiration (22), Gaseous exchange (32), Excretion in humans (32).

nodes.title: Paper 2 — Biodiversity, Ecology and Environment
nodes.description: End-of-year Paper 2 (150 marks): Biodiversity of micro-organisms (29), Biodiversity of plants (29), Biodiversity of animals (18), Population ecology (37), Human impact on environment (37).
